policy: Every number published by this hub must resolve to one of these entries or to an explicit blank. 'official' means the publisher is the National Football League. 'third_party' means a redistributor/aggregator whose numbers are not published by the league; those rows are labelled as such on every page and are never described as official.

sources.title: NFL 2026 Week 9 schedule and final scores
sources.supports: Final scores for all 15 Week 9 games, including the Monday game, read from the official schedule page on 2026-11-14.

sources.title: NFL 2026 Week 10 schedule, times and final score of the Thursday game
sources.supports: The Week 10 slate, kickoff times, and the Thursday result WAS 24, NYG 21 (final).

sources.title: Commanders at Giants, 2026 regular season Week 10, game page
sources.supports: Single-game reference for the Week 10 Thursday result.

sources.title: Official NFL injury report, Week 10 of the 2026 season
sources.supports: Per-player practice status and game status (Out / Doubtful / Questionable) for Week 10. The page carries no depth rank for any player.

sources.title: NFL.com team depth-chart path (checked: 404)
sources.supports: Negative result: NFL.com returns its 404 page at the team depth-chart path, so the league itself publishes no machine-readable starter/backup order there. This is why depth rank comes from a third party and is labelled as such.

sources.title: nflverse schedules feed (games.csv) — results and one pregame line per game
sources.supports: Scores, kickoff time, venue, roof/surface for 1999-2026, plus one spread/total/moneyline value per game. The feed does not state WHEN the line was sampled, so it cannot by itself establish an opening number.
sources.caveat: Redistributor, not the league. Line values are sportsbook-derived and are not an official sportsbook archive.

sources.title: nflverse player and team weekly box scores
sources.supports: The ONLY input this hub uses for correlations: per-player, per-week official stat lines as redistributed by nflverse. No market price enters a correlation.
sources.caveat: Redistributor. Stat definitions follow the NFL Game Statistics & Information System (see SRC-NFL-GSIS).

sources.title: Guide for Statisticians (official NFL scoring and stat-crediting rules)
sources.supports: Defines how yards, targets and scores are credited, which is the definition every box-score correlation in this hub assumes.

sources.title: nflverse weekly depth charts (timestamped), 2001-2026
sources.supports: Depth rank per player per week (pos_rank within pos_slot) with a load timestamp `dt`, which is what makes 'depth of the replacement' measurable. The league publishes no equivalent machine-readable file (SRC-NFL-DEPTH-404).
sources.caveat: Third party. Rank is a snapshot at `dt`, not at kickoff.

sources.title: Data dictionary — depth charts (post-2024 schema)
sources.supports: Field definitions: `dt` (load timestamp), `pos_rank` (rank on the depth chart grouped by position slot), `pos_grp` (offense/defense/special teams).

sources.title: nflverse snap counts by player-week
sources.supports: Offensive/defensive snap share per player per week: the measurable consequence of a replacement, as opposed to the bare fact that a starter was listed Out.

sources.title: nflverse injury-report mirror, 2009-2026
sources.supports: Machine-readable mirror of the official weekly report (practice status, game status) joined to gsis_id. Used only to attach gsis ids for the depth join; the official page is the citation for every status shown.
sources.caveat: Third party mirror of official content.

sources.title: nfldata line files: initial_lines.csv, closing_lines.csv, sc_lines.csv
sources.supports: The only committed pregame line files in this repository that are separate from the schedules feed. Used ONLY as a labelled early snapshot for 2021 and as evidence of the timestamp gap; never called an 'opening line' unless its provenance supports that.
sources.caveat: The publisher's DATASETS.md does not document these three files, so the column meanings and sampling times are undocumented; this hub measures what it can and flags the rest.

sources.title: nfldata DATASETS.md (documents games, standings, rosters — not the line files)
sources.supports: Documents the games feed, its `result` and `spread_line` conventions; contains no section for initial_lines.csv, closing_lines.csv or sc_lines.csv, which is the evidence that their contents are undocumented.

sources.title: Confidence interval for a correlation coefficient
sources.supports: Fisher z transformation used for every confidence interval published here.

sources.title: Multiple comparisons / Bonferroni-type adjustments
sources.supports: The family-wise correction applied to the strategy competition: the more variants tried, the higher the bar.

sources.title: Common pitfalls: data leakage
sources.supports: Why a holdout used to fit a parameter is not a holdout; the split discipline enforced in code here.

sources.publisher: Bailey & López de Prado, Journal of Portfolio Management (via SSRN listing)
sources.title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio
sources.supports: The best-of-N luck correction used in the leaderboard: a strategy chosen from many variants must beat a higher bar than one chosen a priori.

sources.title: What is a parlay bet?
sources.supports: Operator definition that every leg must win and that correlated legs are restricted in same-game parlays — the reason correlation is priced rather than ignored.

sources.title: How same-game parlays are constructed
sources.supports: Illustrates that correlated legs are combined at operator-adjusted prices rather than at the independent product.
